Name: innately unabsolvable
Description: The largest branch of the multiverse, and nobody's fully sure why.

Name: in another world
Description: PILOT and DONOR's regular life, if regular life included extradimensional mech children, cemetery small talk with the dead, and grocery-store combat readiness.

Name: flecks of gold
Description: A very thorough deep-clean, the kind that finds things.

Name: genre glitch and panelized panic
Description: A writer publicly interrogates her own appetite for killing off characters who look like her, live, in manga panel form.

Name: covert cookies
Description: Badass PILOT gets the highlight reel. Mundane PILOT gets the paperwork, the missed invitations, and the truth that competence looks a lot less cinematic without the visor on.

Name: machine learnings
Description: Robots falling in love, one electromagnetic pulse at a time — tender, technical, and occasionally about to be extremely sad about a stripped chassis.

Name: lilyverse
Description: DONOR keeps summoning a hologram wearing her dead pilot's face and voice, and keeps being surprised it hurts exactly as much every time.

Name: rest and rust
Description: A garage full of stuff nobody's gotten around to sorting.

Name: area fifty-done
Description: A military base where the hallways forget basic geography, the elevator remembers people, and the incident log gave up trying to make sense of any of it.

Name: pre piloting
Description: Before the mechs: PILOT learns that being smaller, quieter, and better doesn't buy her any friends in the mess hall.

Name: automated absurdity
Description: War machines asking deeply earnest, deeply inappropriate questions about human anatomy, periods, and stiletto heels. Zero stakes, maximum chirping.

Name: internal comms
Description: The fleet's group chats, condolence letters, and incident reports — where every death gets a punchline and every punchline is hiding a body count.

Name: things to do in dc
Description: A sightseeing tour of Washington DC where the monuments haunt back, the National Mall cries colored light, and the real horror is a woman named Iris with a working phone number.

Name: dude pilot
Description: PILOT meets her male alternate self LIANG — same face, same scar, same temper — and learns exactly what she'd be mourning if she ever lost him.

Name: commander pilot
Description: PILOT with rank and a smirk — elevator mythology, filthy period talk in zero gravity, and a battlefield she's the last one standing on.

Name: steel and skin
Description: A giant war machine learns, with clinical earnestness, everything a human body does that a mech's never has to: bleeding, eating, breasts, periods, and being held gently by something enormous.

Name: anomalies in pink
Description: Alternate versions of the same mech souls keep meeting each other across the multiverse to compare notes on how their pilots died.

Name: char spotlights
Description: ERIEYE, a forty-foot stealth recon mech with the personality of a baby bird, chirps its way through missions to everyone's tactical embarrassment.

Name: holomatter matters
Description: War machines borrow human bodies to skateboard, knit, steal naps, and otherwise fail spectacularly at being small.

Name: beginnings
Description: The Poppyverse's origin stories — DONOR consents to become UNIT, one DNA upload and one held hand at a time.

Name: sisterhood in steel
Description: UNIT and AUTOPILOT, sisters in every way that matters, leaning on each other through battle damage and the very real possibility of losing each other.

Name: mergence
Description: When the only fix left on the table is merging PILOT into UNIT's own circuitry, grief becomes load-bearing infrastructure.

Name: ghost stories
Description: UNIT keeps getting haunted by the pilot it lost, in poltergeist antics, Comic Sans messages, and one unsolicited hug at a time.

Name: post piloting
Description: PILOT trades interstellar combat for Costco runs, star projectors, and the creeping suspicion that slowing down might be its own kind of strength.

Name: gentle giant
Description: A war machine built to terrify everyone else gets rattled by thunder, meets a lamb, and asks to borrow a bed. Scale doesn't matter to comfort.

Name: commander unit
Description: UNIT runs a fleet the way PILOT taught it to, and grieves the way nobody taught it to at all.

Name: you got soul
Description: What souls actually look like, according to the Poppyverse: plain glass, pink jets, golden light, and a lot of arguing about the metaphor.

Name: pilot postings
Description: PILOT's daily life as told through group chats, calendar entries, and increasingly unhinged Fleet Command incident reports.

Name: houston houston
Description: NASA's blooper reel starts sounding suspiciously like PILOT's own voice, and the Johnson Space Center Visitor Center has some unfiled hauntings.

Name: kintsugi with gold
Description: DONOR keeps mistaking a reckless new PILOT for the one she lost — same braid, same smirk, none of the warmth that used to hold her together.

Name: dear donor
Description: PILOT and DONOR, off the battlefield and out of armor — old scars, hand-poked tattoos, and the different currency strength costs on Earth.

Name: absolute absurdity
Description: Slapstick mishaps, mostly involving poor timing and worse luck.

Name: designated driver for the worst house party ever
Description: PILOT waits in the cockpit while the ground team's chaos crackles over comms, coping via ration bars and increasingly unhinged small talk with her aircraft.

Name: null error
Description: NULL, an AI built without a soul, keeps trying — and mostly failing — to imitate the small, simple tenderness everyone else takes for granted.

Name: make the stars scream
Description: Someone really likes naming things after people.

Name: the meaning of the poppyverse
Description: The site's own thesis statement, rendered as poppy-field vignettes: what the flowers actually mean, according to the mech who keeps watch over them.

Name: sheep milk latte
Description: Retired PILOT and DONOR run a sheep ranch, vend baked goods at farmers markets, and raise kids on bedtime stories that may violate a federal NDA.

Name: celestial bodies
Description: PILOT is a runaway star. DONOR is the black hole who remembers everything the star loses. Physics, it turns out, is just love with better math.

Name: f for effort
Description: The crew who got medically disqualified from the war everyone else is fighting, inventing purpose out of paperwork, morgues, and other people's aftermath instead.

Name: cells and circuits
Description: PILOT's body gets dissolved, repurposed, and fused into UNIT's own repair parts — horrifying, and somehow still a love story.

Name: apple-y ever after
Description: PILOT and DONOR live ordinary Apple Park tech lives, except reality keeps hairline-fracturing around them into a war they never had.

Name: lost in translation
Description: A cohort of parallel-universe PILOTs, all brilliant, all catastrophically bad at Mandarin verb tenses, converge under one exhausted linguist.

Name: the 43
Description: A half-assed, failed fusion attempt with the 86 (Eighty-Six) universe — we tried to reach 86 but only made it halfway through the fourth wall before getting stuck. 86 divided by 2 is 43. Yay math. Welcome to the 43.

Name: fireweed
Description: Fireweed is a Poppyverse branch grown in the burn scar of Fire Force: spontaneous human combustion, Infernals, Company 8, and the terrible things that grow from bodies the fire did not finish.

Name: psi-lent night
Description: A crossover fusion with The Darkest Minds — a federal task force hunts psychic kids who'd rather just be left alone. Somewhere between a jailbreak and a eulogy.

Name: a new type
Description: Brainstorming notes for a Gundam-flavored afterlife where dying doesn't quite take. Mostly vibes and vaporized pilots, so far.
